Section 2 • Cosmological Background and Photon Trajectories

2.1 Minimal background cosmology

At the background level, we assume that spacetime is described by a Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) metric. In comoving coordinates, the FLRW line element may be written as \begin{equation} ds^2 = -\cc^2\,dt^2 + a^2(t)\left[ \frac{dx^2}{1-\kappa x^2} + x^2\,d\Omega^2 \right], \qquad \kappa \equiv -\frac{\Omega_k H_0^2}{\cc^2}. \tag{2.1} \end{equation} Here \(t\) is cosmic time, \(x\) is a radial comoving coordinate, \(d\Omega^2\) is the element of solid angle, \(H_0\) is the Hubble constant today, and \(\Omega_{k,0}\) is the present-day curvature density parameter.

The expansion history is encoded in the Hubble function \begin{equation} H(a) = \frac{\dot a}{a} = H_0 \sqrt{ \Omega_{r,0} a^{-4} + \Omega_{m,0} a^{-3} + \Omega_{k,0} a^{-2} + \Omega_{\Lambda,0} }. \tag{2.2} \end{equation}
